name: Bambu Lab P1S

nozzle_reading.method: MQTT push_status after pushall, read at 20:32 UTC

notes.nozzle_material: Was 'hardened-steel', sourced from the vendor spec sheet. The printer itself reports nozzle_type 'stainless_steel' in push_status (S17, 2026-08-02), which is the stock P1S nozzle. The spec sheet describes an option; the telemetry describes this machine. Tray 1 currently holds PLA-CF, which is abrasive and wears a stainless nozzle -- a DFM rule pairing abrasive filament against nozzle material is a Phase 4 candidate and is deliberately not in scope here.
notes.plate_type: The printer-model json declares default_bed_type 'Textured PEI Plate', but that file is not in the machine-preset chain the CLI walks, so a slice defaults to 'Cool Plate' and bakes a 35 C first layer into the G-code. profiles/slicer.json corrects it via preset_overrides (S23).
notes.nozzle_reading: Read again on 2026-10-07 for seanrobertwright/fpv #5: still 'stainless_steel', 0.4 mm. PAHT-CF (GFN04) is abrasive and is not to be printed until a hardened nozzle is fitted and a new reading here says 'hardened_steel'. After a nozzle swap, check that the nozzle type set on the printer or in Bambu Studio matches the fitted nozzle, then read it again. The printer had also moved from the address in .env to a new DHCP lease that day; a DHCP reservation keeps .env valid.

source: build volume and plate geometry from the vendor spec; nozzle_diameter, nozzle_material and plate type measured from this printer's own push_status telemetry on 2026-08-02 (S17), firmware ota 01.10.00.00; nozzle type and diameter read again on 2026-10-07 (fpv #5), unchanged
